A bar trades 40,000 contracts and your platform reports a delta of +6,000. Run the table. Buy volume is (40,000 + 6,000) ÷ 2 = 23,000, sell volume is 17,000, and those add back to 40,000. As a share the delta is 6,000 ÷ 40,000, or +15 per cent, which is a buy share of 57.5 per cent — and 57.5 per cent of 40,000 is the 23,000 you already have.

Read that as shares and the headline changes character. The bar was reported at +15 per cent; what is actually established is somewhere between zero and +25 per cent, a buy share between 50.0 per cent and 62.5 per cent. The bottom of that range is a bar with no imbalance in it at all. The number is not wrong — it is just narrower on the screen than it is in reality, and how much narrower is a property of your instrument that you measured in lesson 7.

And it does not give you a threshold. Whether +15 per cent is a lot depends entirely on what your instrument normally does, and no figure printed here transfers to it. That is a measurement, and problem 3 is how you take it.
